cues.en: This episode of Real Engineering is brought to you by Skillshare, home to over 20,000 classes that could teach you a new life skill. As the world grapples to eliminate fossil fuels from our energy diet, electric cars have seen an incredible boom over the past few years. Last year over 1,000,000 electric cars were sold around the world. The number of Nissan Leafs, Teslas and other electric vehicles in circulation worldwide
cues.zh: 本期《Real Engineering》由 Skillshare 赞助播出，这里有超过 20,000 门课程，能教你掌握一门新技能。随着世界努力在能源结构中淘汰化石燃料，电动汽车在过去几年迎来了惊人的爆发。去年全球电动汽车销量超过了 100 万辆。全球上路的日产 Leaf、Tesla 以及其他电动汽车的总数

cues.en: is now more than 3,000,000.
cues.zh: 现在已经超过了 300 万辆。

cues.en: And while there are many brands of electric car to choose from there are only two choices when it comes to powering electric vehicles, fuel cells or batteries.
cues.zh: 尽管电动汽车的品牌选择繁多，但在驱动方式上其实只有两种选择：燃料电池或电池。

cues.en: Both produce electricity to drive electric motors, eliminating the pollution and inefficiencies of the fossil fuel powered internal combustion engine. Both hydrogen and electricity for batteries can be produced from low or zero carbon sources, including renewable energy like solar and wind, and therefore both are being pursued by car manufacturers and researchers as the possible future of electric vehicles.
cues.zh: 两者都能产生电力来驱动电动机，从而消除了化石燃料内燃机的污染和低效问题。无论是氢气还是电池所需的电力，都可以通过低碳或零碳能源生产，包括太阳能和风能等可再生能源，因此这两者都被汽车制造商和研究人员视为电动汽车未来的可能方向。

cues.en: However, a great debate is being waged by supporters of each technology.
cues.zh: 然而，这两种技术的支持者之间正展开激烈的争论。

cues.en: Elon Musk has called hydrogen fuel cell technology incredibly dumb, claiming they are more of a marketing ploy for automakers than a long term solution. In contrast, Japan has announced its intention to become the world's first hydrogen society,
cues.zh: Elon Musk 曾直言氢燃料电池技术极其愚蠢，声称它们对车企而言更像是一个营销噱头，而非长远之计。相比之下，日本则宣布了打造全球首个氢能社会的愿景，

cues.en: with the Japanese government and the auto industry working together to introduce 160
cues.zh: 日本政府与汽车行业携手合作，计划在 2021 年 3 月之前推广 160 座

cues.en: hydrogen stations and 40,000 fuel cell vehicles by March 2021.
cues.zh: 加氢站并普及 40,000 辆燃料电池汽车。

cues.en: So which is actually better? At first glance hydrogen seems like an extremely clever way to power a car. Compressed hydrogen has a specific energy of nearly 40,000 watt hours per kilogram. Lithium ion batteries at best have a specific energy of just two seventy
cues.zh: 那到底哪个更好？乍一看，氢能似乎是给汽车供能的绝妙方式。压缩氢的比能量接近每千克4万瓦时。而锂离子电池的比能量最多只有每千克270

cues.en: eight watt hours per kilogram, but most fall around 167.
cues.zh: 瓦时，大多数在167瓦时左右。

cues.en: That's two thirty six times as much energy per kilogram for hydrogen,
cues.zh: 也就是说，氢每千克的能量是电池的236倍，

cues.en: and because of its energy density and lightweight nature, compressed hydrogen and fuel cells can power cars for extended ranges without adding much weight. Which as we saw in our last video is a gigantic roadblock for incorporating the technology into the aviation industry.
cues.zh: 而且凭借其能量密度和轻量特性，压缩氢和燃料电池能让汽车实现更长续航而不增加太多重量。正如我们在上一期视频中看到的，这对将该技术引入航空业是个巨大的障碍。

cues.en: The designers of electric vehicles are caught in a catch-twenty two with energy density and range.
cues.zh: 电动汽车的设计者们在能量密度和续航之间陷入了两难。

cues.en: Each extra kilogram of battery weight to increase range requires
cues.zh: 为了增加续航，每增加一千克电池重量就需要

cues.en: extra structural weight, heavier brakes, a higher torque motor, and in turn more batteries to carry around this extra mass.
cues.zh: 额外的结构重量、更重的刹车、更高扭矩的电机，进而需要更多电池来承载这些额外质量。

cues.en: This weight compounding limits how far a battery powered vehicle can travel until new technology can help reduce the weight of the batteries. For hydrogen vehicles this weight compounding is not an issue. Additionally, a hydrogen fuel cell vehicle can be refueled in under five minutes, where a battery powered electric vehicle like a Tesla Model S takes over three hours to fully recharge.
cues.zh: 这种重量叠加限制了电池驱动车辆的行驶距离，直到新技术能帮助减轻电池重量。对氢燃料汽车来说，这种重量叠加不是问题。此外，氢燃料电池车不到五分钟就能加满燃料，而像特斯拉Model S这样的电池电动汽车完全充电需要三个多小时。

cues.en: When looking at the range and refuel times hydrogen can offer, you can see why some car manufacturers are investing in this technology.
cues.zh: 看看氢能提供的续航和加注时间，就能明白为什么一些汽车制造商在投资这项技术。

cues.en: On the face of it, hydrogen is a clear winner, but it falls behind when we start considering the end to end production process.
cues.zh: 表面上看，氢能明显胜出，但一旦考虑端到端的生产过程，它就落后了。

cues.en: While both batteries and hydrogen fuel cells are both forms of electricity storage, the costs differ drastically.
cues.zh: 电池和氢燃料电池都是电能存储形式，但成本差异巨大。

cues.en: Fully charging a Tesla Model three with a 75 kilowatt hour battery costs between 10 and $12 depending where you live. With a rated range of 500 kilometers that's between $2.2.4
cues.zh: 把配备 75 千瓦时电池的 Tesla Model 3 完全充满，根据你所在地区不同，费用在 10 到 12 美元之间。额定续航 500 公里，算下来是 2.2 到 2.4 美分

cues.en: per kilometer.
cues.zh: 每公里。

cues.en: A great price. In a previous video I visited a petrol station that introduced a hydrogen pump, fed by its own on-site production facility,
cues.zh: 很划算。在之前的一期视频中，我参观了一个加油站，它安装了一台加氢泵，氢气由站内自己的生产设施供应，

cues.en: which used off peak electricity to produce hydrogen. The hydrogen from this station cost $85
cues.zh: 该设施利用低谷电制氢。这个加氢站的氢气价格为 85 美元

cues.en: to fill a five kilogram tank of the Toyota Morais on-site,
cues.zh: 才能在现场加满一辆 Toyota Mirai 的 5 公斤储氢罐，

cues.en: which had a range of four eighty kilometers.
cues.zh: 其续航为 480 公里。

cues.en: That's 17.7¢
cues.zh: 也就是 17.7 美分

cues.en: per kilometer,
cues.zh: 每公里，

cues.en: eight times the price. And here lies the problem, hydrogen simply requires more energy to produce.
cues.zh: 是八倍的价格。问题就在这里：制氢本身需要更多能源。

cues.en: To understand the economic viability of hydrogen let's dig deeper into the production process.
cues.zh: 为了理解氢能的经济可行性，让我们深入了解生产过程。

cues.en: Before any hydrogen vehicle can hit the road you first need to produce the hydrogen,
cues.zh: 在任何氢动力汽车上路之前，首先需要生产氢气，

cues.en: but hydrogen is not a readily available energy source. Even though hydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe it is usually stored in water, hydrocarbons such as methane and other organic matter. One of the challenges of using hydrogen as an energy storage mechanism comes from being able to efficiently extract it from these compounds.
cues.zh: 但氢气并不是现成可用的能源。尽管氢是宇宙中最丰富的元素，它通常储存在水、甲烷等碳氢化合物以及其他有机物中。把氢用作储能机制的一个挑战，在于能否高效地从这些化合物中提取它。

cues.en: In The United States the majority of hydrogen is produced through a process called steam reforming.
cues.zh: 在美国，大部分氢气都是通过一种叫作蒸汽重整的工艺生产的。

cues.en: Steam reforming is the process of combining high temperature steam with natural gas to extract hydrogen.
cues.zh: 蒸汽重整是将高温蒸汽与天然气结合来提取氢气的过程。

cues.en: While steam reforming is the most common method of industrial hydrogen production,
cues.zh: 虽然蒸汽重整是工业制氢最常用的方法，

cues.en: it requires a good deal of heat and is wildly inefficient.
cues.zh: 但它需要大量的热量，而且效率极其低下。

cues.en: Hydrogen produced by steam reforming actually has less energy than the natural gas that the steam reforming began with, and while hydrogen fuel cells themselves don't produce pollution,
cues.zh: 通过蒸汽重整生产的氢气，其能量实际上比作为原料的天然气还要少；而且虽然氢燃料电池本身不产生污染，

cues.en: this process does.
cues.zh: 但这个过程会。

cues.en: So if we want to assume a future scenario with as little carbon emission as possible this method won't cut it. Another method to produce hydrogen is electrolysis,
cues.zh: 因此，如果我们想要设想一个碳排放尽可能少未来场景，这种方法是行不通的。另一种制氢方法是电解，

cues.en: separating the hydrogen out of water using an electric current.
cues.zh: 即通过电流将水中的氢气分离出来。

cues.en: While the electricity needed for this process can be provided by renewable sources,
cues.zh: 虽然这个过程所需的电力可以由可再生能源提供，

cues.en: it requires more energy input than steam reforming. You end up losing 30% of the energy from the original energy you put in from the renewables when you carry out electrolysis.
cues.zh: 但它比蒸汽重整需要更多的能量输入。当你进行电解时，你最终会损失掉投入的可再生能源原始能量的 30%。

cues.en: So we are sitting at 70%
cues.zh: 所以算下来，

cues.en: energy efficiency from hydrogen fuel cells, if traditional electrolysis is used, before the car even starts its engine.
cues.zh: 如果采用传统的电解法，在汽车启动发动机之前，氢燃料电池的能量效率就只有 70% 了。

cues.en: A slightly more efficient method of producing hydrogen is polymer exchange membrane electrolysis.
cues.zh: 一种效率稍高的制氢方法是质子交换膜电解。

cues.en: Using this method energy efficiencies can reach up to 80%
cues.zh: 使用这种方法，能量效率最高可达 80%，

cues.en: with the benefit of
cues.zh: 并且它的好处是

cues.en: on-site
cues.zh: 现场制氢——

cues.en: which we will get to in a moment, but this is still a 20% loss of energy from the original electricity from the renewables.
cues.zh: 我们稍后会讲到这一点，但这相比于可再生能源的原始电力仍然有 20% 的能量损失。

cues.en: Some experts say the efficiency of PEM electrolysis is expected to reach 82 to 86%
cues.zh: 有些专家表示，PEM电解水制氢的效率预计将在

cues.en: before 2030, which is a great improvement, but still well short of the batteries charging efficiency at 99%.
cues.zh: 2030年之前达到82%到86%，这是一个巨大的进步，但与电池99%的充电效率相比仍有很大差距。

cues.en: A 19% difference in production costs doesn't explain the difference in costs yet, so where else are we losing energy? The next hurdle in getting hydrogen fuel cell vehicles on the road is transport and storage of the pure hydrogen. If we assume the hydrogen is produced on-site like it was for this petrol station then we eliminate one energy sink, but the cost of storage is just as problematic.
cues.zh: 19%的生产成本差异还不足以解释整体成本的差距，那么我们在哪里还损失了能量呢？让氢燃料电池汽车上路的下一个障碍是纯氢的运输和储存。如果我们假设氢气就像这个加油站一样是在现场生产的，那么我们就消除了一个能量消耗点，但储存成本同样是个大问题。

cues.en: Hydrogen is extremely low density as a gas and liquid, and so in order to achieve adequate energy density we have to increase its actual density.
cues.zh: 无论是作为气体还是液体，氢气的密度都极低，因此为了获得足够的能量密度，我们必须提高其实际密度。

cues.en: We can do this in two ways. We can compress the hydrogen to seven
cues.zh: 我们可以通过两种方式做到这一点。我们可以将氢气压缩到

cues.en: ninety times atmospheric pressure, but that takes energy, about 13% of the total energy content of the hydrogen itself.
cues.zh: 790个大气压，但这需要消耗能量，大约占氢气本身总能量含量的13%。

cues.en: Alternatively,
cues.zh: 或者，

cues.en: we can turn hydrogen into liquid cryogenically.
cues.zh: 我们可以通过低温冷冻的方式将氢气液化。

cues.en: The advantage of hydrogen liquefaction is that a cryogenic hydrogen tank is much lighter than a tank that can hold pressurized hydrogen, but again hydrogen's physical properties means hydrogen is harder to liquefy than any other gas except helium.
cues.zh: 氢气液化的优点是，低温液氢罐比能承受高压的储氢罐轻得多，但同样由于氢气的物理特性，除了氦气之外，氢气比任何其他气体都更难液化。

cues.en: Hydrogen is liquefied by reducing its temperature to minus two fifty degrees celsius,
cues.zh: 氢气是通过将其温度降至零下250摄氏度来液化的，

cues.en: with an efficiency loss of 40% once you factor in the added weight of the refrigerators
cues.zh: 一旦算上制冷设备增加的重量

cues.en: and the refrigeration itself, so pressurization is a better option at a 13% energy loss.
cues.zh: 以及制冷过程本身，效率损失会高达40%，因此能量损失仅为13%的加压方式是更好的选择。

cues.en: Once the hydrogen is produced and compressed to a liquid or gas, a viable hydrogen infrastructure
cues.zh: 一旦氢气生产出来并压缩成液体或气体，可行的氢能基础设施

cues.en: requires that hydrogen be able to be delivered from where it is produced to the point of end use such as a vehicle refueling station. Where the hydrogen is produced can have a big impact on the cost and best method of delivery.
cues.zh: 要求氢气能够从生产地输送到最终使用点，比如车辆加氢站。氢气的生产地点对成本和最佳输送方式有很大影响。

cues.en: For example, a large centrally located hydrogen production facility can produce hydrogen at a lower cost because it is producing more, but it costs more to deliver the hydrogen because the point of use is further away. In comparison, distributed production facilities produce hydrogen on-site,
cues.zh: 例如，大型集中式氢气生产设施可以以较低成本生产氢气，因为产量更大，但输送氢气的成本更高，因为使用点距离更远。相比之下，分布式生产设施在现场生产氢气，

cues.en: so delivery costs are relatively low, but the cost to produce the hydrogen is likely to be higher because the production volumes are less. While there are some small scale on-site hydrogen production facilities being installed at refueling pumps, such as the station mentioned in my last hydrogen video. Until this infrastructure is widespread, we have to assume that the majority of hydrogen is being transported by truck or pipeline,
cues.zh: 因此输送成本相对较低，但生产氢气的成本可能更高，因为产量较少。虽然有一些小规模现场制氢设施正在加氢泵站安装，比如我上一个氢能视频中提到的站点。在这种基础设施普及之前，我们必须假设大部分氢气是通过卡车或管道运输的，

cues.en: where we know that the energy losses can range from 10% up to 40%.
cues.zh: 我们知道能量损失可能从10%到40%不等。

cues.en: In comparison, assuming that the electricity we use for charging the batteries comes from
cues.zh: 相比之下，假设我们用于给电池充电的电力来自

cues.en: renewable resources,
cues.zh: 可再生能源，

cues.en: we just have to consider the transmission losses in the grid. Using The United States grid as a reference for typical grid losses the average loss is only 5%.
cues.zh: 我们只需要考虑电网中的输电损耗。以美国电网作为典型电网损耗的参考，平均损耗仅为5%。

cues.en: So in the best case scenario for hydrogen,
cues.zh: 在氢气的最佳情景下，

cues.en: using the most efficient means of production and transport we lose 20% of energy during PEM electrolysis
cues.zh: 采用最高效的生产和运输方式，PEM电解过程中我们会损失20%的能量，

cues.en: and around 13% for compression and storage, amounting to a 33% loss. In other systems this could be as much as 56%.
cues.zh: 压缩和储存大约损失13%，总计损失33%。在其他系统中，损失可能高达56%。

cues.en: For battery power up to this point we have lost just 6% to the grid and recharging.
cues.zh: 对于电池动力，到目前为止，我们在电网传输和再充电过程中仅损失了6%。

cues.en: Bringing our best case efficiency difference to 27%
cues.zh: 这使得最佳情况下的效率差距达到27%，

cues.en: and our worst case to 50%.
cues.zh: 最差情况下达到50%。

cues.en: The next stage of powering electric vehicles is what is called the tank to wheel conversion efficiency.
cues.zh: 为电动汽车供能的下一阶段被称为“油箱到车轮”的转换效率。

cues.en: For hydrogen fuel vehicles, once the hydrogen is in the tank it must be reconverted into electric power. This is done via a fuel cell which essentially works like a pem electrolyzer but in reverse. In a pem fuel cell hydrogen gas flows through channels to an anode where a catalyst causes the hydrogen molecules to separate into protons and electrons.
cues.zh: 对于氢燃料电池汽车，氢气进入油箱后必须重新转换为电力。这是通过燃料电池实现的，其工作原理本质上与PEM电解槽相反。在PEM燃料电池中，氢气通过通道流向阳极，催化剂使氢分子分离为质子和电子。

cues.en: Once again the membrane only allows protons to pass through it, while electrons flow through an external circuit to the cathode. This flow of electrons is the electricity that is used to power the vehicles electric motors. If the fuel cell is powered with pure hydrogen it has the potential to be around 60% efficient,
cues.zh: 同样，膜只允许质子通过，而电子则通过外部电路流向阴极。这种电子流动就是用于驱动车辆电动机的电力。如果燃料电池使用纯氢供能，其效率潜力约为60%，

cues.en: with most of the wasted energy lost to heat. Like hydrogen fuel cells batteries come with inefficiencies and energy losses. The grid provides AC current while the batteries store the charge in d
cues.zh: 大部分浪费的能量以热量形式散失。与氢燃料电池一样，电池也存在效率低下和能量损失的问题。电网提供交流电，而电池以直流电储存电荷，

cues.en: so to convert AC to DC we need a charger. Using the Tesla Model S as an example, it's peak charger efficiency is around 92%.
cues.zh: 因此要将交流电转换为直流电，我们需要充电器。以Tesla Model S为例，其峰值充电器效率约为92%。

cues.en: The Tesla Model S runs on AC motors,
cues.zh: 特斯拉 Model S 采用交流电动机，

cues.en: therefore to convert the DC current supplied by the batteries to AC current an inverter has to be used with an efficiency of roughly 90%.
cues.zh: 因此，为了将电池提供的直流电转换为交流电，必须使用效率约为 90% 的逆变器。

cues.en: Additionally, lithium ion batteries can lose energy due to leakage.
cues.zh: 此外，锂离子电池可能会因为自放电而损失能量。

cues.en: A good estimate for the charging efficiency of a lithium ion battery is 90%.
cues.zh: 锂离子电池充电效率的一个良好估计值是 90%。

cues.en: All of these factors combined lead to a total efficiency of around 75.
cues.zh: 所有这些因素综合起来，导致总效率约为 75%。

cues.en: However, hydrogen fuel cell vehicles have some of these same inefficiencies.
cues.zh: 然而，氢燃料电池汽车也存在其中一些相同的低效问题。

cues.en: Any kind of electrolysis requires DC current and therefore a rectifier will be required to convert the AC current from the grid to DC. The conversion efficiency here is 92%.
cues.zh: 任何形式的电解都需要直流电，因此需要一个整流器，将电网的交流电转换为直流电，这里的转换效率为 92%。

cues.en: We also need to convert the DC current produced by the fuel cell to AC current to power the motor through an inverter with an efficiency of 90%.
cues.zh: 我们还需要通过一个效率为 90% 的逆变器，将燃料电池产生的直流电转换为交流电来驱动电动机。

cues.en: Finally, the efficiency of the motor must be considered for both the fuel cell and battery powered vehicles.
cues.zh: 最后，无论是燃料电池汽车还是电池驱动汽车，都必须考虑电动机的效率。

cues.en: Currently this is around 90 to 95 for both, which is amazing when you consider that internal combustion engines running on petrol have an efficiency of only around 20 to 30%.
cues.zh: 目前两者的这一效率都在 90% 到 95% 左右，考虑到使用汽油的内燃机效率仅为 20% 到 30% 左右，这个数字相当惊人。

cues.en: If we add up all these inefficiencies and compare current generation batteries to the best and worst case scenario for current gen hydrogen,
cues.zh: 如果我们把所有这些低效损耗加起来，并将当前一代电池与当前一代氢能源的最优和最劣情况进行比较，

cues.en: we can see how they measure up. Even with the best case scenario not taking into account any transport due to on-site production and assuming very high electrolysis efficiency of 80%,
cues.zh: 我们就能看出它们的表现如何。即使在最优情况下（未计入现场生产带来的任何运输损耗，并假设电解效率高达 80%，

cues.en: and assuming a high fuel cell efficiency of 80%,
cues.zh: 同时假设燃料电池效率高达 80%），

cues.en: hydrogen still comes out at less than half the efficiency. The worst case scenario is even worse off. So while you may be able to go further on one fill up of hydrogen in your fuel cell vehicle over a battery powered electric vehicle, the cost that is needed to deliver that one fill up would be astronomically higher compared to charging
cues.zh: 氢能源的效率仍然不到一半。最劣情况则更加糟糕。因此，虽然你的燃料电池汽车加满一次氢气能比纯电动汽车跑得更远，但为了提供这箱氢气所需的成本，与充电相比将高得天文数字般惊人，

cues.en: to these energy losses and inefficiencies.
cues.zh: 这一切都是由这些能量损耗和低效造成的。

cues.en: Based on our worst case scenario we could expect the cost per kilometer to be about 3.5 times greater for hydrogen,
cues.zh: 按最坏情况估计，氢能的每公里成本可能达到约3.5倍，

cues.en: but as we saw earlier it's actually eight times the price, so additional costs of production unrelated to efficiencies are obviously at play. The cost of construction of the facility is one and the profit the station will take from the sale is another. For now these inefficiencies and costs are driving the market, where most investment and research is going into battery powered electric vehicles.
cues.zh: 但前面看到，实际价格是八倍，所以显然还有与效率无关的额外生产成本在起作用。设施建设成本是一方面，加氢站从销售中获取的利润是另一方面。目前，这些低效率和成本正在推动市场，大部分投资和研究都流向了电池驱动电动车。

cues.en: So which wins? Both are equally more green than internal combustion engines assuming equal renewable resources are used to power them. Fuel cells allow fast fill up times and long ranges, a big advantage,
cues.zh: 那么谁胜出？假设都用同等可再生资源供能，两者同样都比内燃机更环保。燃料电池加注快、续航长，这是大优势，

cues.en: but battery powered vehicles might catch up in range by the time there are enough hydrogen stations to make fuel cell vehicles viable.
cues.zh: 但等到有足够多的加氢站让燃料电池车可行时，电池车在续航上可能已经追上来。

cues.en: While fuel cells are efficient relative to combustion engines they are not as efficient as batteries.
cues.zh: 虽然燃料电池相对内燃机高效，但效率不如电池。

cues.en: They may make more sense for operation disconnected from the grid, or as we saw in our last video using hydrogen for planes actually could make a lot of sense, but once again that's a topic for another video. For now battery powered electric vehicles seem to be the sensible choice going forward in the quest for pollution free consumer transport. As battery powered cars become more common, we are also starting to see self driving cars become the norm. If the job of the driver is slowly automated away and consumers have a bunch of free time to read or watch online video,
cues.zh: 它们可能更适合脱离电网运行；或者像上期视频所说，氢能用于飞机其实很合理，不过这又是另一个话题。目前，在追求无污染消费级交通的过程中，电池电动车似乎是合理选择。随着电池车更普及，自动驾驶汽车也开始成为常态。如果司机的工作逐渐被自动化取代，消费者有大量空闲时间阅读或看在线视频，

cues.en: it may be wise to use that opportunity to start learning new skills and Skillshare is a great place to do it. You could take this course on photoshop for beginners and learn a skill that has helped this channel immensely.
cues.zh: 不妨利用这个机会开始学习新技能，Skillshare 是个好去处。你可以上这门 Photoshop 入门课，学一项对本频道帮助极大的技能。

cues.en: You may have noticed we introduced the new thumbnail design for the channel. This was done in part because the channel views were trending downwards for the past two months, despite putting extra effort into production quality. We needed to rethink our strategy for branding and I felt the blueprints strength was that it was easily recognizable as mine, but they also look so similar it's difficult to tell when there is a new video out. So we got to work in photoshop to use the strengths of the blueprint design and build on its weaknesses and we came up with this transitioning effect. Taking designs to reality,
cues.zh: 大家可能注意到了，我们频道换了新的封面设计。部分原因在于，尽管我们在制作质量上投入了更多心血，过去两个月频道的播放量却一直在下滑。我们需要重新思考品牌策略，我觉得之前蓝图风格的优势在于辨识度高，一眼就能看出是我的视频，但也因为太相似，很难让人发现出了新视频。于是我们在 Photoshop 里琢磨，既发挥蓝图设计的优势，又弥补它的短板，最终做出了这种过渡效果：将设计照进现实，

cues.en: which I think fits perfectly with the theme of the channel. We saw immediate effects with the views on our last video jumping 80% compared to our past two month average.
cues.zh: 我觉得这非常契合频道的主题。效果也立竿见影，我们上一期视频的播放量比过去两个月的平均水平暴涨了 80%。

cues.en: This is the power of illustration and you can learn how to use software like photoshop and illustrator on Skillshare.
cues.zh: 这就是视觉设计的力量，你也可以在 Skillshare 上学习如何使用 Photoshop 和 Illustrator 等软件。

cues.en: These days you can teach yourself pretty much any skill online and Skillshare is a fantastic place to do it. With over 20,000 classes ranging from animation, electronics,
cues.zh: 如今你几乎可以在网上自学任何技能，而 Skillshare 是个绝佳的学习平台。这里有超过 20,000 门课程，涵盖动画、电子、

cues.en: programming and much more. The classes follow a clear learning curve, so you can just click and watch without having to curate your own learning experience.
cues.zh: 编程等等。这些课程都有着清晰的学习曲线，你直接点开看就行，不需要费心去自己规划学习路径。
